name: Fuji Foods, Inc.
old_description: IN THE CREATION OF SAVORY FLAVORS FOR THE GLOBAL FOOD INDUSTRY
about:
Fuji Foods USA operates from Browns Summit, North Carolina, as the U.S. subsidiary of Fuji Foods Corporation, a Japanese manufacturer with over 80 years of experience producing soups, sauces, and gravies for Asian markets. The American arm was established to bring that global flavor expertise to domestic food manufacturers and restaurant groups.

The company develops and manufactures custom savory flavors, including concentrated meat bases, broths, yeast extracts, spray-dried powders, and ramen soup bases. Its USDA- and FDA-inspected facilities produce everything from frozen chicken bone broth and shelf-stable beef broth to high-nucleotide yeast extract (HIMAX IG20 DFP) and a library of pre-developed beef, pork, poultry, seafood, and vegetable flavors. Teams also create custom formulas tailored to a customer's budget and target profile.

Fuji Foods serves the global food industry, supplying food-service operators, industrial processors, and restaurant chains that need authentic Asian, American, and fusion profiles. Examples include ramen bases for restaurant groups, marinades and seasonings for entrée producers, and flavor enhancers for soup and sauce manufacturers.

The company differentiates itself by building all meat bases in-house to guarantee batch-to-batch consistency, and by formulating high-intensity flavors that lower usage rates—reducing shipping and storage costs for clients. Collaboration between its U.S. and Japanese flavor teams expands the palette of available profiles, while FSSC 22000, Kosher, USDA, and FDA credentials support regulatory compliance.

name: Fusion Furniture Inc.
old_description: Your home should be a comfortable haven where you can rest and recover, but when you work at home, it…
about:
Fusion Furniture Inc. was founded on May 1, 2009, in Ecru, Mississippi, by Bo and Alison Robbins. After two decades in the furniture industry, the Robbins family set out to create their own line of stylish, value-priced stationery upholstery, building on the region’s generations-long tradition of furniture making.

The company operates over 450,000 square feet of manufacturing space, with an additional 200,000-square-foot factory under construction, and employs more than 500 people. From initial concept to final assembly, Fusion produces American-made sofas and upholstered pieces designed to blend timeless style with affordable pricing.

Fusion’s collections are sold through a network of independent retailers across the United States, Canada, and Mexico. The brand targets residential customers seeking mid-range upholstered furniture, and its wholesale model serves furniture retailers looking for reliable, domestically produced inventory.

The Robbins family emphasizes a “fusion of style, value, and service,” citing above-average customer support and a commitment to community initiatives—including partnerships with the American Cancer Society, I AM ALS, CASA, and the Salvation Army—as core to the company’s identity.

about:
Futaba Corporation of America operates from Huntsville, Alabama. The company's history page suggests a long-standing presence, though a specific founding year is not published. Ownership details are not disclosed in public materials.

The company designs and manufactures OLED displays, TFT-LCD modules, vacuum fluorescent displays, touch interfaces, and both hobby and industrial radio control systems. Its contract manufacturing division provides electronic manufacturing services including surface-mount and through-hole PCB assembly, selective soldering, X-ray and automated optical inspection, in-circuit and functional testing, and custom automation such as robotic conformal coating and semi-automated routing. An in-house machine shop supports rapid tooling and fixture fabrication.

Futaba serves customers in the hobby radio control market, industrial remote-control applications, and OEMs requiring display integration or full-box-build electronics manufacturing. The Mold Marshalling System indicates a focus on injection molding process monitoring for manufacturing environments.

The company emphasizes cell manufacturing to reduce changeover times and eliminate batch processing, and it leverages global technology sharing across Futaba facilities to accelerate adoption of new processes. Custom robotic operations are pursued to improve productivity, quality, and repeatability for client programs.

name: G&G Fabrication and Welding
old_description: , using this technology allows us to create highly accurate and intricate cuts with unique designs, or large-scale production for larger projects.
about:
Founded over 25 years ago in Westfield, Indiana, G&G Fabrication & Welding is a Latino-owned small business led by founders Cesar Guerrero (vice president) and Augusto Guerrero (president). The company began as a custom metal fabrication and light manufacturing shop serving the surrounding communities of Carmel, Noblesville, Fishers, and the greater Indianapolis area.

The shop provides a full range of metalworking services: CNC plasma cutting on an STV table, certified welding (including aluminum), shear and saw cutting, press-brake forming and bending, punching on a GEKA ironworker, and finishing such as powder coating, galvanizing, and sandblasting. They handle projects from one-off custom pieces to larger production runs, managing design through installation under one roof.

Customers span industrial, commercial, and everyday applications. Concrete examples include a custom display sign for Machos Barbershop, a support frame for a large island countertop, trailer repairs, and sprinkle-guard prototypes. The company emphasizes collaboration with other local small businesses and serves both B2B and individual clients across central Indiana.

The Guerrero name — meaning "warrior" — reflects a stated philosophy of tackling any challenge head-on. The firm differentiates itself with end-to-end service, over two decades of fabrication experience, and a commitment to precision equipment and local partnership.

about:
GBS Trend Inc operates a showroom and design team in Los Angeles, California, while its garment production takes place in Turkey. The company traces its legacy to 1974, when it began as a family-owned operation supplying global fashion brands. Today it remains a family-owned private label clothing manufacturer.

The firm specializes in end-to-end apparel production, offering design services, flexible sampling, and a streamlined manufacturing process. Its Turkish factories handle cut-and-sew assembly for private label collections, supported by a Los Angeles showroom that coordinates development and quality oversight. The company also provides PR and marketing services to help brands launch and promote their lines.

GBS Trend serves global fashion brands and emerging labels seeking private label manufacturing. Its customer base includes companies looking for sustainable, ethically produced garments with competitive minimum order quantities. The company emphasizes its experience with international fashion markets and ability to manage production from concept to delivery.

The company highlights its family-owned factory network as a differentiator, citing a commitment to high quality, sustainability, and ethical production. It also points to flexible sampling, competitive MOQs, and a combined design-to-delivery workflow as reasons clients choose its services.

about:
GC Food Factory LLC operates from a facility at 7258 NW 25th Street in Miami, Florida. The company is 100% women-owned, with a majority-female workforce, though its founding year and founders are not publicly disclosed. It began as a food processing plant focused on Latin American culinary traditions.

The manufacturer produces a line of frozen Latin American appetizers, including Venezuelan and Colombian empanadas (offered in beef, chicken, and cheese varieties at 1.5 oz, 3.5 oz, and 5 oz sizes), pastelitos (beef, chicken, cheese at 1 oz, 2 oz, 3.5 oz), and Colombian-style buñuelos (40 g and 60 g). Production is described as artisanal and homemade, using everyday kitchen ingredients, and the plant operates under USDA and FDA certification with strict hygiene and quality monitoring.

GC Food Factory serves food brokers, distributors, and retailers, providing an integrated source-to-delivery solution that can be tailored to customer needs. Its client base spans wholesale and retail channels in the frozen food sector.

The company emphasizes its women-owned status, transparent production processes, and commitment to artisanal quality as key differentiators. It states that its diverse, inclusive team enriches its products and strengthens community ties.

name: GD Process Design, LLC
old_description: Join us this summer at IFT in Chicago, Illinois! Follow the link below and enter…
about:
GD Process Design, LLC is based in Hartland, Wisconsin. The company was founded in 2008 by Lars K. Nielsen, beginning with a focus on service and spare-parts supply for the fats and oils industry before expanding into broader food processing applications.

The firm provides process design, engineering, project management, consulting, and after-sales service for food processing equipment. It engineers and supplies tempering units for product pre‑cooling, pre‑heating, pasteurization, and crystallization, and oversees equipment manufacturing, testing, delivery, installation, start‑up, commissioning, and operator training. Design work uses AutoCAD and SolidWorks for layout drawings, P&IDs, and equipment specifications. A comprehensive in‑stock parts inventory supports quick turnaround on wear and spare parts.

The company serves the food processing, fats and oils, dairy, and pharmaceutical industries. Customers include manufacturers producing butter, margarine, shortening, oils, confections, snack foods, and cryogenic freezing applications. GD Process Design partners with equipment builders such as Gerstenberg Services, Normit, FH Scandinox, FBF Italia, Dohmeyer, FASA, and Primo to supply scraped‑surface heat exchangers, pin‑rotor machines, high‑pressure homogenizers, piston pumps, and cryogenic freezers.

Its mission emphasizes reliable, efficient support across engineering, project management, and after‑sales service, with a focus on flexibility and overseeing every project phase from design through installation.
